row.evidence: Google documents no inbound SCIM endpoint for Workspace; users are created and managed through the Admin SDK Directory API, which "you can use to programmatically create and manage admin-controlled resources owned by a Google Workspace account", and Microsoft's Entra tutorial points its provisioning at that Directory API.
row.notes: Status changed from free (June) to none. The June row said 'SCIM API support available across all paid plans'; no Google page documents a SCIM 2.0 service-provider endpoint for Workspace. IdPs (Entra ID, Okta) provision Workspace through Google's own Admin SDK Directory API, so per the rules this is none with api_provisioning true and api_connector for those IdPs. Microsoft's tutorial calls the prerequisite 'enable SCIM provisioning on G Suite' but the step is API access, and it links the Directory API reference; Okta's OIN page also ticks 'SCIM' (see conflicts). Google also offers vendor-run sync: Google Cloud Directory Sync (from Active Directory/LDAP). Google Workspace is itself an IdP that provisions other apps over SCIM; that outbound capability does not count here. Prices (annual, USD): Business Starter $7, Standard $14, Plus $22 per user/month (rotating introductory discounts for new customers apply to the first users for a limited period), Enterprise contact sales; Business plans max 300 users. June price for Starter ($7) unchanged.

conflicts.text: Microsoft's Entra tutorial tells admins to 'enable SCIM provisioning on G Suite' and Okta's OIN page ticks 'SCIM' for Google Workspace, but Google documents no SCIM service-provider endpoint; Microsoft's own tutorial points the provisioning connector at the Directory API. Vendor (Google) docs used: no SCIM endpoint, API-based provisioning.
